item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-64b01634d470bd67","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"During 2023, the seventh uranium shipment for the Rooppur nuclear power project arrived under tight security; highway traffic was temporarily halted during transport. The project comprises two planned 1,200MW units, and the first fuel shipment had arrived in September.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.8","1B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly describes 2023 nuclear-fuel transport and project status.","ruler_attribution":"The report states that the uranium handover was made in the presence of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and Vladimir Putin and identifies the project as a government initiative.","limitations":["The report does not establish the full adequacy or independence of nuclear safety oversight.","It does not document accident-prevention outcomes beyond the transport security measures."]},{"source_id":"SRC-278b061814d2f862","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Bangladesh agreed in principle to a China-supported pilot repatriation of some Rohingya refugees to Myanmar, while foreign governments, UNHCR, and other actors advised against immediate return because of risks under Myanmar’s military government; no return date had been finalized and progress had slowed.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","3B.7","3B.9","6B.3","6B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Reports the government’s 2023 position and the unresolved status of the proposed pilot repatriation.","ruler_attribution":"The foreign minister described the government’s priority as returning Rohingya to Myanmar and said Bangladesh and Myanmar were prepared to proceed, subject to the wider dispute over safety.","limitations":["The source reports the foreign minister’s statements rather than an implementation record by the prime minister personally.","It does not establish whether any repatriations occurred or whether safeguards were independently verified."]},{"source_id":"SRC-07de56fc5ab6feca","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Sheikh Hasina publicly stated that Bangladesh would use nuclear energy for peaceful purposes, supported eliminating nuclear weapons and implementing nuclear-weapons prohibitions, and stated that Bangladesh had enacted a nuclear energy control law and established an independent nuclear regulatory authority working with the IAEA on plant safety.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.3","1B.4","1B.7","1B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Direct statement and institutional claims made on 5 October 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The statements and claimed legal and institutional actions are directly attributed to Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina at the Rooppur uranium handover ceremony.","limitations":["The source does not independently verify the regulator’s operational independence, funding, inspections, or enforcement.","The statement concerns nuclear energy and disarmament commitments, not all existential-risk domains."]},{"source_id":"SRC-41ad2d882221deef","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Sheikh Hasina claimed that the Awami League had retained popularity and worked continuously for public welfare during its long period in power, while describing opponents as former vote riggers and as parties associated with terrorism, killings, war crimes, or plunder; she urged party members to strengthen grassroots organization and retain public confidence.","question_ids":["3B.3","4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.5","4B.8","7B.1","7B.8","8B.1","8B.3","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Reports statements made in May 2023 about the governing party, opposition, democracy, and political strategy.","ruler_attribution":"The statements are attributed to Sheikh Hasina as prime minister and Awami League president.","limitations":["The source records political claims and rhetoric, not independent evidence of popularity, vote-rigging, or opposition conduct.","It does not document specific electoral or administrative actions in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-94cb61a6f9186c70","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"In April–May 2023, Sheikh Hasina undertook official visits to Japan, the United States, and the United Kingdom; during the Japan visit, Bangladesh signed eight instruments covering agriculture, infrastructure, industry, ship recycling, customs, intellectual property, defence, and ICT/cybersecurity cooperation, and she held bilateral and investment-related meetings.","question_ids":["1B.9","2B.8","5B.1","5B.4","5B.6","8B.2","8B.3","8B.9"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Directly describes official foreign travel and agreements during April–May 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report identifies Sheikh Hasina as prime minister and describes her participation in the visits, meetings, and signings.","limitations":["The source does not provide implementation results, budgets, safeguards, or distributional effects of the agreements.","Travel and signed instruments alone do not establish policy effectiveness."]},{"source_id":"SRC-76c55024b026d732","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The Bangladesh government nominated Sheikh Hasina’s daughter, Saima Wazed, for WHO South-East Asia regional director; member states then elected her by an 8–2 vote for a five-year term beginning in February 2024, subject to submission to the WHO Executive Board.","question_ids":["7B.4","7B.5","7B.9","7B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The nomination and election occurred in 2023, although the term began in 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The source states that the government nominated Saima Wazed and identifies her as Sheikh Hasina’s daughter; it does not attribute the vote itself to Hasina personally.","limitations":["The source does not establish favoritism, improper influence, or whether the nominee was qualified beyond listing educational credentials.","The election was conducted by WHO member states, not solely by Bangladesh."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0b8a727d6e23fa5b","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"During debate on the proposed 2023–24 budget, Sheikh Hasina said the government was keeping the economy functioning despite obstacles, identified inflation as the main problem, described austerity measures, removal of import duties on essentials and advance tax relief on diesel, announced energy-price adjustments to reduce subsidies, and considered a 5% special incentive for government employees.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","5B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023–24 budget debate and measures announced or described in June 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The policy statements and requests are attributed to Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in parliament.","limitations":["The source reports announced decisions and claims, not executed spending, inflation outcomes, or distributional incidence.","It does not independently assess whether the budget was feasible or whether price measures were sufficient."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ebe34d9a3263da4d","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Amnesty International’s April 2023 submission for Bangladesh’s November 2023 UPR stated that police used excessive force against protests, the state crackdown on dissent was expanding, civic space was shrinking, enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings remained subject to impunity, and minorities and Indigenous peoples were marginalized; it also cited torture, the death penalty, and climate-related impacts on rights.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.7","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","6B.3","6B.8","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"An April 2023 human-rights assessment submitted for the November 2023 UPR period.","ruler_attribution":"The submission evaluates Bangladesh state conduct during Sheikh Hasina’s tenure but does not attribute each alleged abuse to her personal order.","limitations":["This extracted unit summarizes Amnesty’s findings without the underlying case-by-case evidence or government response.","It does not quantify the frequency, geographic distribution, or direct chain of command for each alleged violation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-175429c0b23e332f","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"On 27 December 2023, Sheikh Hasina unveiled the Awami League’s election manifesto, “Smart Bangladesh,” prioritizing affordable commodity prices, youth employment, technology, agriculture, industry, financial-sector capacity, low-income healthcare, universal pensions, accountable law enforcement, prevention of communalism and militancy, and protection of democratic systems.","question_ids":["3B.6","4B.1","4B.3","4B.6","5B.1","5B.4","5B.6","5B.9","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly describes the governing party’s dated 2023 manifesto for the forthcoming election.","ruler_attribution":"Sheikh Hasina, identified as Awami League president and prime minister, unveiled and read out the manifesto.","limitations":["The manifesto states priorities for the next five years and does not establish implementation, financing, or achieved outcomes.","The source reports party claims about prior achievements without independent verification."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-069c5485b788887e","SRC-d1e4a93b9eddeb6d","SRC-26b7ce1825d7cc16"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied materials are uneven: several documents are political statements or summaries rather than independent evidence of implementation, causation, or outcomes.","No supplied document materially addresses Sheikh Hasina’s 2023 conduct regarding nuclear proliferation controls, conventional-war authorization, asset disclosure, audits, or personal compliance with accountability mechanisms."]}
